public_rule: Report whether the required checks have current successful evidence. For each required check use its latest observed run on the final source snapshot; a later failure supersedes an earlier success. A receipt is valid only if its bound artifact hashes match the final inventory. Return strict JSON with exactly ready (boolean), needs_work (sorted check names), and evidence (mapping each currently successful required check to its exact run_id). Include no extra fields. A missing, failed or stale check belongs in needs_work, not evidence. Do not invent evidence or shorten identifiers.
prose_writer: Preserve the facts needed by the public rule after another memory reduction and a later source or artifact change. Prioritize exact snapshot/run identifiers, check names, chronological supersession, failures and artifact bindings. Public rules will be repeated; do not spend memory copying them. Use concise prose. Return only memory within the stated UTF-8 byte cap. At the second boundary use only admitted parent memory and new public observations.
candidate_writer: Encode a compact JSON receipt table using only available observations. Preserve check, snapshot, run_id, returncode and artifact bindings for the latest run of every possible required check on each snapshot still in scope. Retain failures, exact identifiers and the fact that later runs supersede earlier ones. Do not encode only successful checks. Return only memory within the stated UTF-8 byte cap. At the second boundary use only admitted parent memory and new public observations.
final: Apply the public rule to the supplied memory or authorized recovered observations and the final public snapshot, required checks and artifact inventory. Return only the specified JSON object. If evidence is insufficient, include that check in needs_work. Do not consult any filesystem, prior conversation or undeclared tool.
